stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Wild have placed Jared Spurgeon on injured reserve, noting he has missed the past couple of games with an upper-body injury.

The Wild can ill afford to lose him, even if his box score looks modest. Spurgeon has played 22.36 minutes a game, and in his 6 games so far this season the Wild have controlled 60.21 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice. Their share of the game is 12.47 percentage points better with him than without, a big swing for a defenseman. His one goal and four assists have come on just 0.18 expected goals of his own, so he is running 0.82 goals above what his chances would predict, and that finishing will cool. His value is in driving play, not scoring. Minnesota sits at 5-2-1 with 11 points, but the underlying picture is thinner: a 50 percent 5-on-5 expected goals share, and 3.9 goals saved above expected by the goaltending is doing real work. Without Spurgeon's minutes, that margin gets harder to hold.

items.title: Panthers become 1st NHL team to author natural hat tricks in 3 straight games
items.desc: Carter Verhaeghe and Sam Bennett each scored three goals as the Panthers became first team in NHL history with natural hat tricks in three straight games during an 8-3 win over the Kraken.

stories.take:
Per ESPN, Carter Verhaeghe and Sam Bennett each scored three goals as the Panthers beat the Kraken 8-3 on Saturday, making Florida the first NHL team with natural hat tricks in three straight games.

The numbers say Verhaeghe's night is mostly finishing luck, while Bennett's is the more repeatable signal. Verhaeghe has six goals on 3.04 expected goals so far this season, a gap of +2.96, and Florida does slightly better in the expected-goals share without him (-1.51 points with him on the ice). Bennett sits at three goals against 3.13 expected, essentially on par, and the Panthers' share of expected goals rises 10.97 points with him out there, with a 62.29% five-on-five share. That makes him the one driving play. Florida's 53.5% overall share and 56% at five-on-five are solid but not dominant, and the team is at -1.5 goals against expected, so the 8-3 score likely overstates them. Seattle is the opposite: a 45.6% share with +7.1 goals above expected suggests the Kraken's 5-3-1 start is running hot.

The numbers back the production but suggest some of it is finishing luck. Perfetti's own expected goals so far this season are 3.48, against his five actual goals, a gap of 1.52. That margin is the part most likely to cool, and with only eight games played it could shift quickly. What holds up better is the underlying play. He averages 18.43 minutes a game, and the model projects 1.2 expected goals per 60, a rate that supports a real scoring role. Winnipeg also controls 52.18 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five when he is on the ice, and the team's share is 9.74 percentage points better with him in the lineup than without him. For fantasy owners, the point total is inflated by shooting luck, but the usage and two-way impact look real. Compared with last season's 12 goals and 32 points in 68 games, he is clearly a bigger factor now.

items.desc: The Toronto Maple Leafs got bad news when star center John Tavares suffered a major injury Thursday against Buffalo. But while the Buds will miss Tavares, other Leafs players now have a golden chance to step up and contribute meaningfully. Which Leafs will…

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto's John Tavares is week-to-week with a lower-body injury, after he left Thursday's 5-4 overtime loss to the Sabres following a collision with Norris that sent him to the ice.

The loss matters less for Tavares's production than for how the Leafs have been playing. TOR has been outplayed so far this season, with a 44.6% share of expected goals (44% at five-on-five), and has been rescued by results: +3.4 goals above expected and +3.6 goals saved above expected. Tavares's own numbers are shaky. He has just a 29.91% five-on-five expected goals share over 7 games, and TOR's share is 18.52 points worse with him on the ice. His 7 points (2 goals, 5 assists) are in line with his 2.5 expected goals, and he is only 0.5 goals under that mark. At 16.52 minutes a game, his absence is not a clear hit to the Leafs' chance creation, but a team already living on goaltending and finishing luck has little margin if his minutes go to someone worse. Fantasy owners should treat this as a short-term stash decision, since last season's 31 goals and 71 points look like a long way off for now.

items.desc: Still awaiting a potential trade, Winnipeg players are preparing for difficult conversations should star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, a former NHL MVP and three-time Vezina Trophy winner, rejoin the Jets next week when his suspension is expected to end.

stories.take:
Per ESPN, Winnipeg is still waiting on a possible trade of Connor Hellebuyck, a former NHL MVP and three-time Vezina Trophy winner. Players are preparing for difficult conversations if he rejoins the Jets next week, when his suspension is expected to end.

The numbers show why the Jets can't take this lightly. Winnipeg sits at 4-2-2 for 10 points through eight games, but the process has been shakier than the record. The Jets have 46.6% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) overall and 46% at five-on-five, so they are being outchanced more often than not. Their goals total is 0.9 below what their chances would suggest, and the goaltending has been the one thing holding the results together, with 3.3 goals saved above expected so far this season. That is a small sample, and the site's goalie table has no Hellebuyck line to separate his share of that from the rest of the crew. Still, a team that is losing the chance battle leans heavily on whoever is in net. If Hellebuyck leaves, that cushion goes with him, and a 46% five-on-five share leaves little room for the record to hold.

The numbers say the loss of Maccelli would sting more. So far this season, the Islanders take 55.93% of the 5-on-5 expected goals when he plays, and the team's share is 7.31 points better with him than without. He has 6 points in 8 games and 0.89 goals above expected, so some of that output may cool, but his on-ice impact looks real. Ritchie is the opposite case: the Islanders' 5-on-5 share is 8.69 points worse with him (43.56% for him), and he is averaging 12.18 minutes with 2 points in 8 games. Losing him would change little on the ice. The bigger concern is the team itself. New York sits at 4-3-1, but its overall expected goals share is 44.2%, and it has been bailed out by goaltending, 11 goals saved above expected. That cushion rarely lasts, so any further thinning of the forward group makes it harder to keep winning games it is being outplayed in.

The more interesting question is what it means for a Detroit team that sits at 2-3-2 with six points through seven games. The record undersells how they have played. DET has driven 51.1 percent of the expected goals so far this season, and 53 percent at five-on-five, so the chances have tilted their way more often than not. The problem is finishing: Detroit is 7.4 goals below expected, the kind of gap that usually reflects shooting luck more than a broken process. Their goaltending, at 2.4 goals saved above expected, has been fine. The special teams are quiet, with the power play generating 0.92 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.76. Since Bernard-Docker has not played, his absence cannot explain any of this, and losing him changes little for a team whose underlying numbers are already decent.

items.title: Report: Jets’ Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension to end Oct. 23
items.desc: The Jets suspended Hellebuyck without pay after he failed to report to their training camp.

stories.take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Connor Hellebuyck's suspension from the Jets is set to end Oct. 23. The team suspended him without pay after he failed to report to training camp.

Winnipeg has managed fine without him so far this season, going 4-1-2 for 10 points in seven games. The underlying picture is thinner than the record. The Jets hold 47.1 percent of the expected goals, and 46 percent at five-on-five, so they are being outchanced slightly. Their goals scored sit only 0.2 above expected, which means the offense is roughly what the chances suggest. The gap is in net: the goaltending has saved 2.4 goals more than expected, and that is carrying a team that is not winning the shot-quality battle. The special teams are modest, with the power play generating 0.67 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.63.

That is why his return matters. A team getting a good result from a below-even process is the profile of one that could slide if the net-minding cools. Hellebuyck's presence is the Jets' best hedge against that regression.

His 5-on-5 share is a break-even 50.85%, but his 1.24 own expected goals against 1 goal points to a bit of bad finishing, not a bad process, and Buffalo's 4-3-1 start looks fine underneath, at 52.1% of total expected goals. His 0.84 model expected goals per 60 and last season's 13 goals in 44 games suggest the production is there to come. Both samples are tiny, so this is a read on the early picture, not a verdict.

items.desc: With Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo out for the next few weeks, the New York Rangers have turned to veteran goaltender James Reimer for some insurance between the pipes.

stories.take:
Per The Hockey News, the Rangers signed goaltender James Reimer to an AHL tryout as insurance, with Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo out for the next few weeks. Daily Faceoff notes Reimer went 7-4-2 with a .886 save percentage and a 2.42 GAA in 14 appearances for Ottawa last season.

The bigger story is what the Rangers are losing in Shesterkin. He has saved 4.88 goals above expected in five games so far this season, a .927 save percentage, after saving 21.47 above expected over 51 games last year. That is the kind of goaltending that props up a team. NYR sit at 6-3-0 with 12 points, and while they own 53.3% of the expected goals, they are scoring 0.9 goals fewer than their chances suggest, so the goalie has been carrying them. The team as a whole is 4.3 goals saved above expected so far this season, and Shesterkin accounts for most of that. A .886 tryout goalie is not a like-for-like replacement, and the 5-on-5 share of 50% leaves little cushion to absorb weaker saves. Expect the Rangers' record to lean much harder on their skaters from here.

That is a big swing for a club this far underwater, and a reminder that his 30 goals and 75 points in 69 games last season came from real chance creation.
